item.title: Ocarina of Time Suggests a Majora’s Mask Remake Is Only a Matter of Time
item.description:
Ocarina of Time’s new remake includes several subtle nods to Majora’s Mask. Find out how these characters, mechanics, and Nintendo's history point toward a potential Majora's Mask remake.

The New Ocarina of Time Teases Majora’s Mask Connections


Returning Characters Look and Sound More Like Their Sequel Selves


The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake seems to lay the groundwork for a possible Majora’s Mask remake, although the company has yet to announce one. Released in 2000, Majora’s Mask is a direct sequel set several months after Ocarina of Time. It follows the same young Link and Epona into Termina, where the Happy Mask Salesman asks Link to recover the powerful mask Skull Kid stole.
The strongest evidence for a Switch 2 remake comes from the Happy Mask Salesman, a minor shopkeeper in Ocarina of Time who becomes a central figure in its sequel. His latest model wears gold cuffs absent from both earlier versions of Ocarina of Time, but present on him in the Nintendo 64 and 3DS versions of Majora’s Mask.
Additionally, his rewritten dialogue and considerably more unsettling presentation bring him closer to being the mysterious figure waiting inside the sequel’s Clock Town’s tower than the eccentric merchant of the first game.
Skull Kid is another recurring character who becomes the sequel’s central antagonist under the influence of Majora’s Mask. In the remake, players found that hitting him with the slingshot reportedly triggers the distinctive cackle he uses in Majora’s Mask, which was absent from any version of Ocarina of Time.

The Passage of Time is Central to the Sequel


Another reference appears when Link speaks to a Zora while wearing a mask. The Zora says, "Although I have heard tell of other cultures that make use of masks in their rituals." The remark echoes an early scene in Majora’s Mask, after Link returns to the Clock Tower without recovering the stolen mask. The Happy Mask Salesman then explains its history, describing Majora’s Mask as an accursed artifact once used by an ancient tribe in hexing rituals.
Encountering the Running Man while wearing the Bunny Hood reveals another connection. He describes it as the ears of a legendary rabbit "said to move like the wind," recalling its function in Majora’s Mask, where it increases Link’s running speed. Ocarina of Time doesn't grant Link the same benefit, but after the Running Man buys it, he sprints off much faster than before.
Also, a new feature of the Ocarina of Time remake is that the clock continues running inside towns and dungeons, with residents moving between their homes, workplaces, and evening routines as the day progresses. A more elaborate version of that idea sits at the heart of Majora’s Mask, which unfolds across a repeating three-day cycle in which every resident follows a set schedule.
However, speaking to Game Informer ahead of the remake’s release, Aonuma said staff members had asked about adding nods to Zelda’s timeline and references to other games. He recalled telling them, "No, let’s focus on this game. Let’s make this the best version of Ocarina of Time that we can." Although the timeline remained in the back of the team’s mind, Aonuma said the remake was not dealt with the intention of explicitly referencing other entries.
Still, the team managed to slip in subtle connections like Sheik's harp consistent with the one seen in Skyward Sword.

Nintendo Has Paired These Two Zelda Games Twice Already


Majora’s Mask Followed Ocarina of Time on N64 and 3DS


A new Majora’s Mask remake would follow a familiar pattern, as Nintendo has previously followed Ocarina of Time with its sequel. Majora’s Mask wasn't planned while Nintendo was developing Ocarina of Time.
Speaking with then-Nintendo president Satoru Iwata in a 2010 Iwata Asks interview about Super Mario Galaxy 2, Shigeru Miyamoto explained, "For Majora’s Mask, we simply adopted the 3D engine from Ocarina of Time." Nintendo reused that engine, along with many of the earlier game’s character models and underlying systems, before building a new world around its repeating three-day cycle.
Years later, Nintendo took a similar route with the 3DS remakes. Ocarina of Time 3D launched in June 2011, and work on Majora’s Mask 3D began "almost immediately" after development wrapped. Grezzo handled both remakes, although the second remained unannounced for more than three years. Nintendo finally revealed it in November 2014 and released it the following February.

Nintendo Rarely Lets a Good Foundation Go to Waste


Nintendo tends to build new games on existing foundations, carrying over engines, visual styles, and core systems rather than starting from scratch. Spirit Tracks retained Phantom Hourglass's touch-controlled framework, and Tears of the Kingdom retained Breath of the Wild’s version of Hyrule while redesigning Link’s abilities. Grezzo also returned for the Switch remake of Link’s Awakening, whose visual and gameplay approach later became the starting point for Zelda’s adventure in Echoes of Wisdom.
Additionally, after completing Super Mario Galaxy 2, Miyamoto proposed another because Nintendo had invested so much time in an engine that could serve as the foundation for a follow-up. Development began under the working title Mario Galaxy 1.5, with plans to reuse the original game’s spherical environments and finish the project within a year.
It eventually grew into a full sequel developed over two and a half years, with Miyamoto estimating that more than 90% of its courses were new. In Iwata Asks, Satoru Iwata connected the approach directly to Zelda, saying, "That’s been one of Miyamoto-san’s methods ever since we followed up Ocarina of Time with Majora’s Mask."
Ocarina of Time is widely regarded as one of the most influential games ever made, while Majora’s Mask never achieved the same mainstream reach. Its darker, more experimental approach has nevertheless earned it a devoted following among Zelda fans.
With Nintendo reporting a "very strong start" for the remake, the connections between the two games have once again left players looking beyond Hyrule toward Termina, and upward at the prospect of its unsettling moon rendered in the remake’s upgraded visuals. item.title: Nintendo Adds Game Gift-Giving Feature in eShop
item.description:
Nintendo will add a gift-giving system to the Nintendo eShop starting November 16th, 2026, allowing family group members to purchase digital games for one another.

Nintendo Introduces Digital Gift-Giving in eShop


From Family to Family Member


Nintendo adds a new gift-giving feature to the Nintendo eShop just in time for the holidays. The feature is set to go live on November 16th or 17th, 2026, depending on the eShop’s region, with the update for it now live on all devices ahead of its launch.
Eligible games, DLCs, and upgrade packs can be gifted by anyone to any family member in a family group they are a part of.
However, not all products may be gifted, and will depend on the developer or publisher’s individual discretion, and the number of digital gift purchases in a given time period (as of writing, still unannounced) is limited. Additionally, supervised accounts (restricted accounts usually given to children) are not allowed to send digital gifts.

Gifts Appear As Presents on the Home Screen


A fun feature of the gift-giving system is that after purchasing, it will appear immediately at the HOME page of the recipient’s device (or chosen device, if there is more than one) in the form of a wrapped gift box. The color of the gift box can be chosen between eight colors. Once received, it can be downloaded and played right away. Gifting a Nintendo eShop product can be done on the product page of any eligible game, DLC, or upgrade pack. After the feature is launched, a “Give as a Gift” checkbox will be available.
Nintendo closed off the announcement post with a “This feature is a great way to celebrate a special occasion with your kids. Happy gifting!” message, opening up a new avenue for gift giving during the holiday season.

Community Reactions Mixed, Hoping For Friends List Expansion


Response to the news has been mixed, with some people appreciating the upcoming feature, creating an avenue for families who may not have the luxury of being physically together during the season and are in long-distance relationships.
Majority of the community found it lacking, especially because it was only limited to the Nintendo family group, which has a maximum of eight people. Many have wished for it to extend to the player’s friend list, similar to other popular platforms like Steam which allow for gifting to not only friends but even strangers.
Others have said that it doesn’t completely beat the notion of physically opening gifts during the holidays, and since the post specifically mentioned gifts to kids, they thought that it would defeat the purpose of gift-giving.
Source:
Official Nintendo Site: Coming soon: Gift digital games to family group members

item.title: WoW Forever Casts Solo Leveling’s Aleks Le as Every Male Skyborne NPC
item.description:
WoW: Forever casts Solo Leveling star and prominent voice actor Aleks Le as two named characters and every male Skyborne NPC. Find out more about his announcement and his other roles across anime and games.

WoW: Forever Gave Aleks Le a Much Bigger Role Than He Expected


Le’s Voice Runs Through Two Named Characters and Every Male Skyborne NPC


World of Warcraft: Forever (WoW: Forever) has tapped Aleks Le, the English voice of Solo Leveling protagonist Sung Jinwoo, to voice Talaanis Shadowsong, Rorian the Dayseeker, and every male Skyborne NPC in the game. Le revealed his involvement in an X (Twitter) post on November 5, one day after Blizzard’s anticipated reimagining of WoW’s original Azeroth launched globally.
"I had no idea the extent of my role," Le wrote, expressing surprise that his work went beyond two named characters to include every male Skyborne NPC. This gives Le a recurring presence in Zephras Isle, the Skyborne starting zone created for the new playable race, and wherever they may be throughout Azeroth. "I’m honored to be part of this legendary title."

Aleks Le Has Become a Familiar Voice Across Newer Anime and Games


Le is a Los Angeles-based voice actor whose work spans anime and video games. He considers Zenitsu Agatsuma in Demon Slayer his first major role, describing it as his "first-ever gigantic role in terms of status and scope" in an interview with TheWrap. Since then, he has also lent his voice to Sung Jinwoo in Solo Leveling, including the action-RPG Solo Leveling: ARISE OVERDRIVE, Jiji in Dandadan, Thorfinn in Vinland Saga’s Netflix dub, and Manjiro "Mikey" Sano in Tokyo Revengers.
Gamers might recognize Le as Luke in Street Fighter 6, protagonist Makoto Yuki of Persona 3 Reload, Daredevil in Marvel Rivals, Mark Grayson in Invincible VS, and Sonon Kusakabe in Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade.
Players who purchased the Skyborne Heroic Pack ($29.99) or a higher-tier edition will hear plenty of Aleks Le as they journey from Zephras Isle into the wider world of Azeroth. Check out our review for WoW: Forever below:

item.title: FF7 Remake Producer Still Wants a Screen Adaptation Nearly 30 Years After Directing the Original
item.description:
FF7 remake producer Yoshinori Kitase wants to see more Final Fantasy adaptations. Find out why he thinks that the remakes could inspire a new series based on the games.

Final Fantasy Producer Is Open to More TV Adaptations


Kitase Points to FF7’s Expanded World


Yoshinori Kitase, producer of the Final Fantasy VII remake (FF7) trilogy, would like to see more Final Fantasy stories on television. He sees the world Square Enix expanded in the remakes as a starting point for future adaptations.
When IGN asked at Lucca Comics & Games 2026 whether Square Enix was still interested in film and other adaptations, Kitase said the remakes explored far more of FF7's world than the original game. He said he’d welcome "games or TV series inspired by the story of Final Fantasy."
In the past, he raised the idea of a FF7 film or TV show in January 2025, telling Danny Peña on Gamertag Radio that he’d heard about Hollywood directors and actors who played the game, calling the prospect of seeing one of those creators make an adaptation "strictly my personal sort of wish."

The Cycle of Influence From Star Wars to Expedition 33


In IGN’s interview, Kitase pointed out how Final Fantasy developed its own style by bringing influences from Japanese manga and anime into its early European-inspired settings. He’d spoken with the creators of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, Sandfall Interactive, and was happy to see how they’d drawn on Final Fantasy to make a game of their own.
The producer described it as a "cycle where we inspire each other," recalling how George Lucas’s Star Wars films influenced his own work. He even named Biggs and Wedge in Final Fantasy VI after two Rebel pilots. Additionally, the podrace in The Phantom Menace also gave him the idea of putting a sport inside a fantasy world, which led to Blitzball in Final Fantasy X.
Kitase said he and other developers who worked on the 1997 original still felt strongly about FF7. The remakes gave them a chance to build something new around it and let new players discover what longtime fans loved. For him, much of the series’ appeal comes from watching its characters change over the course of a game. When asked to pick a favorite among the games he’d worked on, he said 7 might be "the one I feel more attached to."

Final Fantasy’s Films Found Their Footing With Advent Children


Advent Children’s Ties to the Remake Trilogy


Final Fantasy has told stories outside the games for decades, starting with the 1994 anime Legend of the Crystals, which returned to the world of Final Fantasy V two centuries after the game. Its first theatrical film, 2001’s Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within, was such a box-office flop that it made Enix think twice about a merger it was already considering with Square, according to former Enix chairman Yasuhiro Fukushima in a 2003 interview with Mainichi Interactive, as reported by RPGamer.
Despite that, the companies went ahead with the merger in 2003. Two years later, Square Enix returned to film with Advent Children, a sequel to FF7 in which a mysterious illness and the return of old enemies draw Cloud Strife out of seclusion. It became a home video hit, with Sony Pictures Home Entertainment reporting 4.1 million copies shipped by 2009, when the expanded Advent Children Complete arrived on Blu-ray.
It’s still Final Fantasy’s most successful film project, and nearly two decades after its original release, Square Enix brought the expanded cut to U.S. theaters the week before FF7 Rebirth launched in 2024. It even influenced the upcoming finale, as Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi told Anime News Network at Tokyo Game Show 2026 that the team had "definitely added connections to Advent Children," alongside ties to Crisis Core and other FF7 titles.
As the remake trilogy draws to a close in 2027, Kitase sees room for more Final Fantasy adaptations. After more than a decade spent expanding the world of FF7, it's up to him whether he still has a story to tell in Midgar or explore one of the series' other worlds. item.title: NIKKE Offers 20 Free Pulls and an Apology Following PC Launcher Malware Attack
item.description:
NIKKE officially apologized with in-game compensation and added a scanner after its PC launcher was used to spread malware since October 30. Find out what publisher Level Infinite says happened and what players can do.

Level Infinite Apologizes and Releases Its Timeline of the NIKKE Launcher Attack


PC Players May Have Been Compromised Since October 30


Goddess of Victory: NIKKE has issued a public apology on its official X (Twitter) account after confirming that attackers tampered with files used in the game’s PC launcher. In the November 5 statement, publisher Level Infinite took responsibility for the security failure and acknowledged that the incident put players’ computers and personal information at risk. "An official program intended to let players enjoy the game should never become a threat to their safety," the NIKKE Operations Team wrote.
Developer Shift Up CEO Kim Hyung-tae issued a separate apology on November 4, saying the developer was working with Level Infinite and "dedicating all our resources to identifying a fundamental solution." Meanwhile, players received in-game compensation; X users under the post shared a screenshot of the in-game compensation notice, listing 3,000 Gems, 10 Advanced Recruit Vouchers, and a bundle of upgrade materials. These materials and gems should cover 10 pulls, and the vouchers for another 10, for a total of 20. Players can use either on limited-time banners like the ones NIKKE ran during its Persona crossover.
Image taken from NIKKE's official website
According to Level Infinite, an as-yet-unknown third party took control of a domain used by some of its game services on September 27. Later that day, four scripts the launcher downloaded from the publisher’s servers were altered. According to their timeline, those scripts began delivering malware to players’ PCs on October 30 at 3:52 a.m. (UTC+9), a day after the fourth anniversary update launched. The team says it detected the tampering around midnight on November 4, replaced three of the scripts within a few hours, and refreshed the server cache for the fourth time later that day.
However, independent researcher MotherSphere cited a player’s launcher log indicating that the remote-access malware had already run on October 23 UTC, or October 24 at 1:40 a.m. in the time zone Level Infinite uses. In this timeline posted on November 4, the reported case started more than six days before the publisher’s stated start date.

Official PC Launcher Adds a Malware Scanner


Level Infinite Will Review Reports of Financial Loss


Level Infinite says the current version of NIKKE’s PC launcher is safe to use after the company fixed the affected files and ran additional checks. It is asking anyone who opened the Windows launcher at least once since September 27 at 3:41 p.m. (UTC+9) to check their PC and accounts. Fortunately, the publisher confirms the native Android and iOS versions were unaffected.
On their end, the November 5 update added a scanner that checks for malware tied to the incident when players start the Windows client. If the scan detects the malware, the client asks for permission to remove the associated files and registry entries. Players who have already uninstalled the launcher, or who prefer to check without reopening it, can follow NIKKE’s manual guide on their website.
Alongside the in-game rewards announced for all players, Level Infinite is asking anyone who suspects an account with another service was compromised or who suffered a financial loss to contact customer support. "We will review each inquiry carefully and respond as promptly as possible," the publisher wrote, as its investigation into the extent of the damage is ongoing.
Despite Level Infinite’s assurances, players are understandably frustrated that opening the official PC launcher left them checking their PCs for malware and wondering what happened to their personal information. For more on the game itself, check out our Goddess of Victory: NIKKE review below.

item.title: God of War Laufey Delayed to May 20, 2027 to Reach Its "Fullest Potential"
item.description:
God of War Laufey has been delayed to 2027. Learn more about the delay and the upcoming God of War game's release date.

God of War Laufey Release Moved to May 2027


Faye's Journey Through Everywhen Needs More Development Time


God of War Laufey will now launch on May 20, 2027, three months later than its previously announced February 16 release date. Santa Monica Studio confirmed the delay on November 4 and said the team needs more time to complete development and push it to "its fullest potential." The studio thanked fans for their patience and promised to share more updates soon.
Since it was first revealed during the PlayStation State of Play June 2026, GoW Laufey was met with a lot of criticism, mostly due to it being a God of War title not being headlined by Kratos. Recently, fans also came down on the GoW Laufey Collector Box being priced at $149.99 and not including the actual game.

Dodging a Loaded February 2027 Lineup


While some were disappointed with the delay, other fans were glad that GoW Laufey's release date will be moved further. Players noted that February 2027 is already jam-packed with big titles, and the upcoming GoW spin-off deserved its own spotlight.
Several JRPGs, such as Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United and Atelier Karia: The Night Kingdom & the Guide of Memories, will be launching that month, along with highly anticipated remakes like Persona 4 Revival and Yu-Gi-Oh! Tag Force GX. Additionally, major franchise titles like Metro 2039 and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis are also releasing in February, and the month will be capped off by what is probably the biggest game of the month: the open-world action-RPG reboot of Fable.
Santa Monica Studio has been quite busy with the God of War franchise, with its most recent launch being God of War: Sons of Sparta in February 2026. They are also currently in production on a God of War trilogy remake, which will see the return of Kratos' original voice actor, TC Carson. To find out more details about God of War: Laufey, check out our article below.
Sources:
Santa Monica Studio X post on God of War Laufey Release Date Delay

item.title: Honkai: Nexus Anima Launches Spring 2027 with Final Beta Test Coming November 25
item.description:
HoYoverse announced that Honkai: Nexus Anima is scheduled to release in Spring 2027. Get the latest on the game’s release window and the upcoming final beta test.

Honkai: Nexus Anima Release Window and Final Beta Test Announced


Official Release in Spring 2027


Honkai: Nexus Anima (HNA) will launch in spring 2027, the game's official X (Twitter) account announced. Players can now pre-register for iOS on the App Store, which lists the mobile title as expected to go live on April 1, 2027, though HoYoverse has not confirmed this exact release date.
It has been over a year since HoYoverse first teased HNA during Honkai: Star Rail’s Concert livestream in May 2026. The open-world creature-collector auto-battler generated significant buzz for featuring a blend of original characters with familiar faces from across the Honkai universe, including Honkai Impact 3rd's Kiana Kaslana.
The developers subsequently conducted multiple closed tests, including the Nexus Bond and Evolution tests, which introduced new gameplay features and expanded the roster of playable characters.

Final Beta on November 25


Aside from the official release window, HoYoverse also revealed that the Final Beta for HNA will begin on November 25, 2026. The announcement came with a short teaser titled "Get Nexergized!", which promotes the in-game flagship Nexergy sports drink of the Fleming Collective.
It features several characters, including Juelle, Gloria, Nanafey, and Otto, playing various sports and quenching their thirst with the product. Even Novarchs like Blade and Bai Mei are shown enjoying the energy drink in battle.
In a follow-up post on X (Twitter), HoYoverse shared additional details regarding the upcoming Final Closed Beta. Players are guaranteed to obtain the featured 5-Star Eidos along with their Anima Companion on their first 50/50. Additionally, reaching Player Level 40 will grant them with 5-Star Eidos: Blade and his corresponding Anima Companion.
The Final Beta also introduces Juvenile Anima that travel alongside your character and evolve from fledgling stages into fully grown forms, while also adding more rare Chromatic variants to spot in the open world. Players can also rest at their RV anytime and build habitats for their Anima to relax and explore.
Furthermore, the beta will introduce higher-difficulty challenges and unique boss fights to test players' skills. It will also debut the all-new Nexus Arena, a competitive PvP game mode where Animasters can build custom lineups, battle matched opponents, and climb ranks.
The HNA Final Beta will be a limited data-wipe test and will be conducted on PC, iOS, and Android. Those who are interested can pre-register on the game's official website until November 22, 2026, at 9:59 UTC+8 (November 21, 2026, at 8:59 PM ET/5:59 PM PT).
Fans who will be selected for the test will be notified through a dedicated test access link and via the email they provided at registration. To know more about Honkai: Nexus Anima, check out our article below.

item.title: WePlay Expo JAPAN 2027 to Host AAA and Indie Game Demos at Makuhari Messe in April
item.description:
WePlay Expo JAPAN 2027 will take place in Chiba from April 2 to 4, with hands-on game demos, themed exhibits, and stage programs planned for the event. Check out the event schedule and the activities planned for visitors.

What is WePlay Expo?


A Long-Running Games Exhibition in China Since 2017


WePlay Expo is the biggest indie game exhibition in China, and has been hosted in China every year since 2017. Although it's known as an indie exhibition, the event is known for bringing games of all times, including upcoming AAA games, for players to enjoy on-site.
The most recent WePlay Expo, hosted in Shanghai in 2015, clocked over 20,000 guests, with over 500 titles exhibited for play from over 300 studios.

WePlay Expo Japan 2027 Plans Hands-On Demos and Gaming Cultural Activities


Organizers Outline Play Areas, Themed Exhibits, and Community Programs


WePlay Expo JAPAN 2027 will bring the China-born gaming culture event to Japan for the first time from April 2 to 4, 2027, at Makuhari Messe (Halls 5 and 6) in Chiba. First held in Shanghai in 2017, WePlay Expo focuses on hands-on game demos. Plans for the event in Japan include playable titles across PC, console, and mobile platforms.
Japanese companies IID and Sanei have formed the WePlay Expo JAPAN Organizing Committee. CiGA (China Indie Game Alliance), one of the organizations behind WePlay Expo in China, will be the licensor and producer of the event in Japan.
The organizers want visitors to have enough time to try the games that interest them. Alongside demos at exhibitor booths, an organizer-run demo area is planned to help attendees discover unfamiliar titles. The lineup is expected to span major AAA releases and indie games, though specific titles have yet to be announced.
The exhibition will include gaming hardware and peripherals, with themed displays planned for the venue. Exhibitors will be able to sell merchandise directly from their booths. The organizers are developing stage programs that may include new game announcements or updates, demos, and speedrun events. Tournaments and talks with developers and creators are among the other proposals, though the organizers have yet to finalize the schedule and formats.
Outside the exhibition floor, the organizers plan to develop themed experiences around popular game franchises, with special events and guest programs under consideration. Exclusive merchandise and novelty items are planned as part of these experiences. The event will provide opportunities to discover emerging game developers and student creators, with fan communities across different genres invited to gather and share their interests. Plans for an industry networking space include media representatives, influencers, and creators working across fields such as music, illustration, and scenario writing.
WePlay Expo JAPAN 2027 aims to connect the gaming community across borders by bringing developers and players together and helping Japanese creators reach overseas audiences. A dedicated business program is planned to give industry professionals opportunities to meet potential partners and explore international collaboration.

WePlay Expo JAPAN 2027 Targets 20,000 Visitors


According to the organizers, the 2025 Shanghai event attracted more than 20,000 visitors and featured over 500 game titles, with participation from more than 13 countries and regions. It also hosted over 300 exhibitors, 14 stage programs, and more than 10 themed areas.
For WePlay Expo JAPAN 2027, the organizers have set a target of 20,000 visitors. The three-day event will run as follows:
  • Friday, April 2 (Business Day): 1:00 P.M. to 5:00 P.M. JST. Access is limited to guests, media, trade visitors, and business-ticket holders. An industry after-party is planned for 5:30 P.M. to 7:00 P.M. JST.
  • Saturday, April 3 (Public Day): 9:30 A.M. to 6:00 P.M. JST
  • Sunday, April 4 (Public Day): 9:30 A.M. to 5:00 P.M. JST

Paid tickets are planned for general visitors and business attendees on the public days. Ticket prices and sales dates have not yet been announced. The organizers note that event plans and specifications remain under development and may change. Further updates will be available through the official WePlay Expo JAPAN 2027 website.

item.title: The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel Title and Logo Officially Revealed After 8 Years
item.description:
Bethesda Game Studios has finally given The Elder Scrolls 6 a name. Learn more about what was revealed here!

The Elder Scrolls 6 Official Name Revealed


“The Next Journey to Tamriel Will Be in The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel“


The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel is the official title of Bethesda Game Studios' long-awaited next entry in the RPG series. Bethesda revealed the name in a video celebrating the studio's 40th anniversary, where director Todd Howard described the occasion as the "perfect time" to announce the title.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma also shared the same sentiment on X (Twitter), congratulating both past and present members of the studio. Bethesda then followed up with another post, thanking fans for over "40 years of shared memories."
The reveal has been a long time coming. Bethesda first announced the game at E3 2018, more than eight years ago. The studio has yet to share further details about the game, and the announcement did not include new gameplay footage, a release date, or confirmed platforms.

Not Releasing Anytime Soon


While the official title and logo generated significant hype among fans of the franchise, Bethesda noted on their follow-up X (Twitter) post that it will be some time before they share more details. Bloomberg's Jason Schreier doubled down on this on his Bluesky post, and stated that TES6 could still be more than two years away from releasing.
He reminded fans that the Elder Scrolls sequel was announced alongside Starfield in 2018 to appease the community on the controversial launch of Fallout 76. Todd Howard even stated earlier this year that he wished that fans would just "forget" that the game was announced. Since the reveal, information about the game's development has been scarce, and the biggest technical detail the developers have shared was that they will be adding a fan as an NPC.
In November 2025, Todd Howard stated that TES6 is "still a long way off", and hinted that it could be shadow-dropped, just like what they did with The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion. However, the director assured fans on December 2025 that development is "progressing very well", and that the game is taking most of the studio's manpower.
This was reiterated in Bethesda's July 2026 press release, where the developers noted that the sequel is their "primary development focus today", and understood that fans have been waiting a very long time for the game. "The next chapter is on the way. We’re where we planned to be, loving how it looks, and playing it every day," Bethesda stated.
Sources:

item.title: Dragon’s Dogma 2 x Delicious in Dungeon Collab Adds Laios and Marcille as Pawns
item.description:
Dragon’s Dogma 2 teams up with Delicious in Dungeon, letting players recruit two members of the anime’s adventuring party. Find out how to get Laios and Marcille, claim their outfits, and when the crossover ends.

Delicious in Dungeon Comes to Dragon’s Dogma 2


Laios and Marcille Can Join Your Party


Dragon’s Dogma 2 has collaborated with Delicious in Dungeon (Dungeon Meshi), bringing Laios and Marcille into the action RPG as recruitable Official Pawns. As announced by developer Capcom on their website and social media on November 4, it arrived alongside Title Update 4.2 on the same day for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam, with the Nintendo Switch 2 version following on November 12.
Players can recruit recreations of Laios and Marcille from Riftstones located in towns and other settlements. Once hired, they function as support Pawns and can accompany the Arisen and their Main Pawn during their adventures. The crossover trailer casts Laios as a Fighter, placing him on the front line with a sword and shield, while Marcille appears as a Sorcerer who uses offensive magick spells.
Capcom has also added outfit sets inspired by the two characters, and players who logged in during the collaboration period will automatically receive these outfits in their player storage. Both the Arisen and their Pawns can wear the collaboration outfits, and any outfits claimed during the event will remain available after the collaboration ends.
The crossover is available in both the base Dragon’s Dogma 2 and Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen. According to their announcement post on X (Twitter), the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Steam versions will offer the content from November 4, 2026, until the January 29, 2027 update. The Nintendo Switch 2 version will run from November 12 until the same update. Laios and Marcille can only be recruited during this period.

Dragon’s Dogma Has a Long History of Anime Crossovers


Official Pawns Were Previously Used for Creator Collaborations


Before bringing licensed characters into the game, Dragon’s Dogma 2 primarily used its Official Pawn system for collaborations with real-world personalities. Capcom created recruitable Pawns based on content creators like Maximilian Dood, Asmongold, and FightinCowboy, as well as athletes from different regions, such as football star Shinji Kagawa and Japanese national volleyball players Yuki Ishikawa and Ran Takahashi.
Dark Arisen expanded the lineup with more international creators and characters from Capcom’s Capcom Collectibles videos, including funny depictions of Toy Leon from Resident Evil, Knockoff Ryu from Street Fighter, and the nightmare-inducing Real Rudy from Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection, showcasing the felyne Palico companion as an uncanny human.
The wider series has previously crossed over with several anime and manga properties. The first Dragon’s Dogma partnered with Berserk: The Golden Age Arc, adding weapons and armor modeled after Guts and Griffith. Berserk later returned for another series collaboration with the Japan-exclusive Dragon’s Dogma Online in 2018.
Dragon’s Dogma Online, which shut down in 2019, also collaborated with Attack on Titan and Overlord. The Attack on Titan event offered Survey Corps equipment, while the Overlord crossover added armor based on Ainz and Albedo, themed furniture, and a limited in-game event.
Dragon’s Dogma 2 and Delicious in Dungeon are a natural fit, with both following fantasy adventuring parties through monster-filled worlds where a good meal can make all the difference. Delicious in Dungeon fans ready to embark on their own adventure can check out our Dragon’s Dogma 2 Dark Arisen review below.

item.title: NIKKE PC Launcher Files Were Reportedly Compromised for Over a Month to Spread Malware
item.description:
NIKKE’s PC players who opened the launcher on or after October 23 may have been exposed to malware. Find out what happened and how Level Infinite responded.

NIKKE PC Launcher Reportedly Used to Deliver Malware to Players


Attackers Modified Files on Level Infinite’s Official Network


The Goddess of Victory: NIKKE PC launcher is reportedly compromised and used to distribute remote-access malware. Independent security researcher MotherSphere published a report on GitHub on November 4, documenting the incident using launcher logs, cached files, live server responses, and evidence submitted by other players. The official X (Twitter) account of NIKKE also confirmed that the PC Launcher's script files were tampered with by a third party, but client fixes and an update were already implemented, and that further details will follow.
According to the GitHub report, four JavaScript files hosted on Level Infinite’s official content delivery network (CDN), a network of regional servers that delivers launcher files directly to players, were modified on September 27. When the NIKKE launcher loaded the altered files at startup, hidden code could contact an outside server and download a remote-access agent, a type of malware that lets an attacker control parts of an infected computer from another location.
Images taken from MotherSphere’s post on GitHub
Once installed, the malware could reportedly run commands, browse and download files, and take screenshots of every connected monitor. Its available commands also included access to saved browser passwords and data stored by browser-based cryptocurrency wallets. These functions show what the malware could do, although investigators have not confirmed what information it actually took from each affected computer.
The apparent access to Level Infinite’s CDN has also led players to question whether other Level Infinite games such as PUBG Mobile, Delta Force, Honor of Kings, Arena Breakout, Age of Empires Mobile, and Undawn could be at risk. However, the investigation has only documented malware being delivered through NIKKE’s PC launcher. Still, many players are avoiding those titles until the situation is resolved.

Evidence Suggests the Malware Was Active Before the Anniversary Update


Level Infinite Appears to Have Quietly Replaced the Compromised Files


The earliest reported instance of the malware actually running on a player’s computer dates to October 23, meaning it was active before NIKKE’s fourth-anniversary update launched on October 29.
The technical report indicates that Level Infinite had already begun replacing the affected files. Three of the four compromised files were replaced with clean copies during the early hours of November 4. The main copy of the fourth file had already been cleaned on October 28, but two regional CDN servers continued distributing an older compromised copy for several more hours.
This means that players in different locations could temporarily receive different versions of the same file. Replacing the files on Level Infinite’s servers would also stop only new infections. It would not remove malware that had already reached a player’s computer.
Current reports are limited to the PC launcher, with no evidence that the native Android or iOS versions were affected. For more on the game itself, check out our Goddess of Victory: NIKKE review below.
Source:
NIKKE PC launcher compromise (November 2026)

item.title: Petit Planet Is Coming to Switch 2 in 2027 Before Genshin Impact Ever Made It to Switch
item.description:
HoYoverse confirms Petit Planet is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027. The free-to-play cozy life sim launches on PC, iOS, and Android on December 4, with Switch 2 details to follow.

Petit Planet Switch 2 Port Confirmed for 2027


We Got Petit Planet on Switch 2 Before Genshin Impact on Switch


Petit Planet is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027, which would make it HoYoverse’s first release on a Nintendo platform. The announcement arrives years after the publisher’s biggest hit, Genshin Impact, was promised a Switch version that never materialized.
HoYoverse revealed the news during its Petit Planet Pre-Launch Special Program on November 1. The game’s official X account followed with a post that read, "Let’s meet in the Starsea!" and carries the hashtags #PetitPlanetSwitch2 and #PetitPlanet1204. The announcement refers only to Switch 2 and mentions no version of the original Nintendo Switch. HoYoverse has named the year and has not yet shared an exact date.
HoYoverse has announced a Nintendo release before. In January 2020, months before the game’s launch, miHoYo announced a Switch version of the open-world action RPG Genshin Impact and shared a trailer for it on the official Genshin Impact YouTube channel. The game later released on PC, PlayStation, and mobile, but the Switch version still hasn't appeared nearly seven years later. Fans have joked about the missing port ever since, and the gag remains one of the community’s best-known memes.
The trailer’s comment section reflects that. Years after it went up, viewers still return to leave jokes about the long wait, from yearly "anniversary" greetings to Titanic-style "it’s been 84 years" quips and puns on the trailer’s "Coming Soon" tagline. Many commenters pointed out that the Nintendo Switch 2 arrived before Genshin Impact reached the original Switch, while others have said they gave up on the port long ago.

Petit Planet Launches on PC, iOS, and Android on December 4, 2026


Players on other platforms will get the game first. According to HoYoverse on an official X post, the worldwide release takes place on December 4, 2026, for PC, iOS, and Android as a free-to-play game.
Earlier this year, HoYoverse held Petit Planet’s second closed beta test called Stardrift Test, which, although a data-wipe test, allowed participants to keep specific chat history from the Café Untamed private room. After the testing ended, the developers thanked players who joined and promised to address their feedback to better the game.
Ahead of the official launch, HoYoverse has scheduled a pre-launch live stream titled “Petit Planet: Moving Preparation Special” for December 3, the day before release, which gives players a final look at the game. Anyone who wants to see more before the stream can check out our review of the Stardrift test below.

item.title: Ocarina of Time Remake Reimagines Hyrule With Help From Its Original Artist
item.description:
Ocarina of Time’s remake brings back an illustrator from the Nintendo 64 original to create a new map. Find out how Nintendo plans to preserve Hyrule's new look while preserving its sense of discovery.

An Original Ocarina of Time Illustrator Returns for the Remake’s New Map


Veteran Zelda Artist Yusuke Nakano May Have Returned


Ocarina of Time remake’s new map was drawn by the artist who created illustrations for the Nintendo 64 original. Director HokWai Ng, who first worked on the Zelda series in Tears of the Kingdom, confirmed this detail in the second part of Nintendo’s Ask the Developer interview posted on Nintendo's blog on November 2. However, the company didn’t name the returning artist.
The strongest candidate is Yusuke Nakano, a veteran Nintendo illustrator who joined the company in 1992 and led the founding game’s character illustration work. He later contributed to other Zelda titles like Majora’s Mask, the Oracle games, The Wind Waker, and Twilight Princess, handling main character design and illustration.
His later Zelda credits include Skyward Sword, A Link Between Worlds, Tri Force Heroes, Breath of the Wild’s Ganon battle artwork, and the 2019 Link’s Awakening remake. Recently, he was credited as a field artist on 2025’s Kirby and the Forgotten Land: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World, suggesting that he has remained active at Nintendo.

The Remake’s Map Preserves The Feeling of the Classic


While recent Zelda games use large, seamless environments, the remake still divides its world into separate maps, preserving each location's identity and how the areas connect. The team wanted to update Hyrule’s presentation without losing the pacing created by leaving one distinct region and entering another.
Ng used the route from Kokiri Forest, past the Great Deku Tree, and into Hyrule Field as an example. "We wanted each new area to bring the same air of excitement that players experienced in the original. We hoped that moving from one map to another would provide a natural point of transition, giving players a chance to reflect on their adventure so far while building anticipation for the next part of their adventure awaiting them in the next area," he said.
Recent previews suggest Nintendo has modernized movement within those boundaries; major regions remain separated, but players can enter shops and other interiors without loading screens. Our own observations noted familiar areas like Kokiri Forest had subtle changes like a new training area in the shop and a new monument in front of the Castle Town gates.

Bigger Landmarks, But Clearer Boundaries


Extra Warp Points Were Removed to Keep Players Exploring Hyrule


The team still needed to make Hyrule feel richer on modern hardware without suggesting that every visible location could be reached. Art director Aya Shida said this became especially challenging in Hyrule Field, saying, "We wanted to preserve how it felt to explore the original map while using today's visual capabilities to make the world denser and more detailed."
To solve this, the artists added more detail to explorable spaces and reduced visual information in inaccessible areas. Distant environments therefore read as background scenery, allowing the remake to create a denser world without misleading players about where they can travel. Nintendo also deliberately enlarged landmarks such as Hyrule Castle and the windmill so players could read them more easily from a distance.
The importance of reading and traveling through Hyrule also affected the remake’s proposed fast travel system. Producer Eiji Aonuma initially requested additional warp points, but playtesting showed that the shortcuts caused players to miss discoveries along the way. "We were missing out on the moments of discovery that came from stopping along the way and wondering, ‘Wait, what’s this?’" Aonuma explained. He ultimately asked the team to remove all the new warp points.
Despite that, Nintendo has still added changes to the remake, such as integrating it with a smartphone or adding a new area where players can rematch defeated bosses.
Nintendo is going to great lengths to preserve what made exploring Hyrule so memorable in the original game, adding modern features while showing restraint over what it changes. With Yusuke Nakano speculated to be the returning illustrator, the new map could represent his modern reinterpretation of the Hyrule he helped define nearly three decades ago.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is releasing soon on November 5, 2026, exclusively on the Nintendo Switch 2. There's also a special 40th Anniversary Switch 2 edition and Ocarina of Time Amiibo with bonus in-game cosmetics.
Sources:
Ask the Developer Vol. 24: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — Part 1
Ask the Developer Vol. 24: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — Part 2

item.title: Silver Palace Releases Worldwide December 14; Free 4-Star Character Available at 30M Pre-Registrations
item.description:
Silver Palace launches worldwide on December 14, 2026 on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. A free 4-star character is up for grabs if the pre-registration milestone campaign reaches 30 million.

Silver Palace Launches December 14 With a Free 4-Star Up for Grabs


Silver Palace Arrives Simultaneously on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android


Silver Palace has an official launch date, and a free 4-star character is waiting for players if the game’s pre-registration milestone campaign hits its top tier. The open-world detective action RPG will release worldwide on December 14, 2026, which gives fans a little over a month to get ready for the city’s mysteries.
The date was revealed through the game’s official social media account, which teased the launch with the line “This is the golden age for detectives.” Publisher Elementa followed up with a press release confirming that the game will release simultaneously across regions at 2026/12/14 (UTC+8). Silver Palace will be available on Android, iOS, PC, and PlayStation 5 at launch, so players can pick the platform that suits them best.
The game is built on Unreal Engine 5 and will support 12 languages at release. Pre-registration is open on every platform, and the campaign attached to it gives the community a clear reason to sign up before the countdown ends.

Pre-Registration Rewards Include a Free 4-Star Character at 30 Million


The Pre-Registration Milestone Event is already live and rewards players based on the combined follower count across the game’s official social media channels. According to the announcement, reaching the 30-million milestone unlocks a free 4-star character. The rewards also include 20 Simulation Shots, the game’s pull currency for its character recruitment system.
Elementa’s press release states that Silver Palace has already passed 15 million global pre-registrations. That puts the community at roughly the halfway point of the top milestone, with several weeks of growth still ahead before launch. Each tier unlocks as the community reaches the matching number, so every new follower and sign-up moves the rewards closer for everyone.
Pre-registering is free and can be done through the official Silver Palace website or through the game’s storefront pages. Following the official social accounts also contributes to the milestone count, which makes sharing the campaign one of the easiest ways to push the total higher.
Silver Palace is an open-world detective action RPG published by Elementa. The game launches worldwide on December 14, 2026 (UTC+8) on Android, iOS, PC, and PlayStation 5, with support for 12 languages. Pre-registration is open now through the official website and each platform’s storefront.

item.title: Death Stranding Isolations Anime Announced for 2027 Disney+ Release With a Story Set After the Games
item.description:
Kojima Productions has unveiled DEATH STRANDING ISOLATIONS, a hand-drawn Death Stranding anime that follows a girl who shuns human contact in an America reconnected by Sam.

Death Stranding Isolations Anime Arrives on Disney+ in 2027


Kojima Productions Reveals the Story and Setting in a Teaser Trailer


DEATH STRANDING ISOLATIONS takes the world of Death Stranding into anime form and will stream exclusively on Disney+ and other Disney services.
The series was announced on October 29 through a teaser trailer on Kojima Productions’ official YouTube channel. The video’s description says “that world expands into new frontiers,” referring to the shattered setting Hideo Kojima created in the original game.
In the same description, the synopsis opens with the line “My mom became a crater.” It refers to the Death Stranding, the chain of catastrophic explosions that occurred when the dead crossed into the world of the living. Many survivors were forced into absolute isolation afterward, and the series centers on one young girl among them. She grows to prefer her solitude and avoids every opportunity for real human connection.
The story takes place in North America immediately after Sam, the game’s protagonist, reconnects the continent through the Chiral Network. The renewed connections bring “new and unforeseen consequences,” and the series follows several people who chose a different path from Sam and his Bridges comrades. They include an old man who connects people through a method that “defies all reckoning,” a female soldier “ensnared in a cycle of war and destruction,” and a boy who “seethes with rage at the absurdity of his life.” Chance encounters then launch the girl into a world she does not recognize.

Takayuki Sano and E&H Production Lead the Anime


Takayuki Sano directs the series, with animation by E&H Production. The studio’s earlier work includes NINJA KAMUI, BULLET/BULLET and the Magic Knight Rayearth television series, and the trailer description calls the result world-class hand-drawn animation. The cast, episode count and exact premiere date have yet to be announced.
Sources:
Kojima Productions, “DEATH STRANDING ISOLATIONS | Teaser Trailer,” official YouTube channel, published October 29, 2026

item.title: This Week’s Gaming News Roundup: Oct 25th to Oct 31st
item.description:
← Previous Week
(Oct 18th - Oct 24th)		This Week
(Oct 25th - Oct 31st)

October comes to a close with plenty of movement in the industry. It brought a new December release date for HoYoverse’s Petit Planet and an animated continuation of the Death Stranding universe. The Duskbloods has been delayed to 2027, and the future of established games also came into focus through an approaching service shutdown and a change in publishing. Several featured stories turned to the friction between developers and their communities, particularly when plans for PvP and endgame progression run against what players want from a game. These developments have plenty of time to unfold, and the conversations surrounding them will carry well beyond October.
Whether it's sinking 300 hours into a single campaign or diving into a mammoth expansion, this week’s games prove that scale only works when backed by depth. Rich character arcs give new weight to classic journeys, and tight combat mechanics make deep investment feel worthwhile. Where things stumble, however, is in sluggish grinds and half-baked survival features that fall short of their ambition.
Regardless, here’s a quick look at some of the week’s biggest gaming headlines.
Gaming News At A Glance
Petit Planet Launches This December
Death Stranding Isolation Anime Teaser Trailer Revealed
The Duskbloods Release Delayed To Further Enhance Core Concepts
Phantom Blade Zero Protagonist Soul Is Now Voiced by Sonic
Palworld’s Pocketpair Open to Releasing the Game on Switch 2
Other News and Developments This Week
Review Roundup: Oct 25th to Oct 31st
Good at What They Do, Less Sure of What Comes Next
  • ANOMALITH
  • Phantom Blade Zero
  • Monster Hunter Outlanders

Other Reviews This Week

Gaming News At A Glance: Petit Planet Release Date Announced, Death Stranding Gets an Anime, The Duskbloods Delayed, Phantom Blade Zero Protag VA Recasted, Palworld Switch 2 Is a Possibility


Petit Planet Launches This December


Petit Planet will officially launch on December 4, 2026, for iOS, Android, Epic Games Store, and Windows PC, with pre-downloads opening on December 1. Pre-registration is now available through the official website, where sign-ups receive a Bestie Star-Light.
Additional rewards will unlock as global registrations reach new milestones, with the final reward being a Sproutling Outfit at 10 million registrations. HoYoverse will also host a Pre-Launch Special Program on November 1, with more rewards and surprises teased for the broadcast.

Death Stranding Isolation Anime Teaser Trailer Revealed


Kojima Productions announced Death Stranding Isolations, a new anime set to stream exclusively on Disney+ and other Disney services in 2027. Set in North America after Sam reconnects the continent through the Chiral Network, the series explores the consequences of restoring those connections through the lives of people who chose paths different from Sam and his Bridges comrades. Its story centers on a young girl who prefers isolation and avoids human contact. Her encounters with several other survivors eventually draw her into an unfamiliar world.
Takayuki Sano directs the anime, with E&H Production handling animation. The studio previously worked on NINJA KAMUI and BULLET/BULLET. Kojima Productions revealed the project through a teaser trailer on October 29, though the voice cast, episode count, and exact premiere date remain unannounced.

The Duskbloods Release Delayed To Further Enhance Core Concepts


FromSoftware has pushed The Duskbloods out of its planned 2026 release window, with the Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive now targeting 2027. Feedback from the August network test has given the studio more to address in its eight-player PvPvE matches, where players earn Victory Points through direct confrontations or by outmaneuvering their rivals. Some boss encounters also encourage temporary alliances between competing players. FromSoftware plans to use the extra development time to refine these non-combat strategies and the rules governing each match. A specific release date has yet to be announced.

Phantom Blade Zero Protagonist Soul Is Now Voiced by Sonic


Roger Craig Smith is now the English voice of Soul, the former elite assassin at the center of Phantom Blade Zero. Best known for voicing Sonic the Hedgehog since 2010, Smith has also played Ezio Auditore in Assassin's Creed and Batman in Arkham Origins. His casting replaces Jay Maksenuk, whose performance appeared in earlier trailers and preview footage. S-GAME has yet to explain the change ahead of the game's release.

Palworld’s Pocketpair Open to Releasing the Game on Switch 2


Palworld could eventually make its way to Nintendo Switch 2, as Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe has reiterated the studio's interest in the platform. In an October 27 interview with VGC, he praised the console as an "amazing platform" for Japan's game industry and said Pocketpair would love to discuss a potential release. No Switch 2 version has been officially announced.
Pocketpair previously considered Nintendo hardware as a potential home for the game, and the studio has also expressed interest in expanding to more handheld devices. A Switch 2 release remains possible, with further details depending on future discussions between the studio and Nintendo.

Other News and Developments This Week


  • Pokémon UNITE’s End of Service Coming in 2027, and Players Are Disappointed
  • Blue Archive JP’s Publisher Switch to Nexon in January 2027 Brings Mixed Reactions
  • Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen Could’ve Been So Much Better If It Was Strictly Post-Game Content
  • Aniimo is Pushing for PvP in its Next Update, But Players Don't Want It
  • Poppy Playtime Chapter 6: Are Escape From Playtime Players Building A Better Place?
  • Aniimo Is Getting PvP, But Can The Community Handle The Toxicity?
  • Aniimo's Endgame Direction is Alienating its Core Community, and the Oct 29 Update Might Make it Worse
  • Aion 2’s Healer Shortage Starts With How It Treats Clerics
  • Silver Palace Releases Worldwide December 14; Free 4-Star Character Available at 30M Pre-Registrations

Review Roundup: Oct 25th to Oct 31st


Good at What They Do, Less Sure of What Comes Next


A game's strongest idea can make a lasting impression, even when the rest of the experience struggles to keep pace. This week's reviews have some interesting examples, from a monster-hunting game that gets the thrill of the chase right to a survival-horror shooter whose gunplay deserves better systems around it. A new expansion gives an already enormous adventure room to grow, and a long-awaited story finally brings its central character's past into focus. But the difference lies in how well each game turns its best ideas into an experience worth remembering.

ANOMALITH


An apartment block with inverted gravity and a shopping street that repeats endlessly are among the spaces Reona Minazuki explores in ANOMALITH. The third-person survival shooter follows her work as a Diver for the government’s Anomaly Zone Countermeasures Office. She joined to find her missing friend Arisa, and each expedition takes her deeper into these warped spaces to fight their inhabitants and recover materials for weapon and gear upgrades.
The best part of ANOMALITH is easily its gunplay. Deciding which threats to take down first and picking off weak points makes every firefight feel sharp, and there’s plenty of room to mess around with different builds. Reona's arc and the shady agency behind her ground the story nicely, but the campaign wraps up so fast that major reveals barely have room to breathe. Plus, once you get overpowered, the actual scares stop landing entirely.

Phantom Blade Zero


In Phantom Blade Zero, Soul has 66 days to clear his name after being framed for his master's murder. His search for the truth takes him across the Wulin, a martial world where traditional kung fu shares the stage with industrial machinery and mechanical horrors. Its kungfupunk setting gives the journey an industrial edge that feels tailor-made for an extravagant martial arts film.
Phantom Blade Zero knows exactly how cool it wants Soul to look. Its cinematic boss fights can escalate from tightly choreographed duels to spectacle bordering on the absurd, and its wide weapon selection gives the combat plenty of personality. The forgiving difficulty and extensive accessibility options make it an inviting entry point for newcomers; genre veterans may find the action too lenient. The main story is easy to follow, though its expanding cast and dense terminology muddy some developments. For S-Game, whose earlier releases were largely mobile games, this is a remarkably polished debut with plenty of promise for what comes next.

Monster Hunter Outlanders


Radiantite gives Aesoland an unusual ecology, with the island's deposits linked to a new class of monsters known as Radiant Species. Monster Hunter Outlanders builds its mobile hunts around this setting, pairing familiar weapons with original Adventurers whose specialized skills change how each weapon plays. Players explore the island, hunt its monsters, and gather materials to develop their roster.
The combat gets the fundamentals right. Monster attacks are satisfying to read and respond to, and the Adventurers give players a good reason to try different approaches to a hunt. The monster designs also translate well to mobile. Aesoland's mystery keeps the main story moving, though the Bond episodes mostly recount individual backstories and leave the cast short on chemistry. Developing several Adventurers takes considerable time and resources, with materials, Zenny, and Energy making roster progression a persistent grind.

item.title: New Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Commercials Show Off Ganon With His Organ and Flashy Combat Footage
item.description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake received two official commercials ahead of its release. Find out more about the new footage it includes.

Ocarina of Time Remake Gets Two Commercials Ahead of Its November 5 Release


Ocarina of Time Remake Recreates Ganondorf’s Dramatic Boss Fight


The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has received two official commercials ahead of its release. Posted on Nintendo Japan’s X (Twitter) account on October 16 and detailed on their website, the first video, titled "Ocarina," revisits footage previously shown in trailers. However, the "Battle" commercial features mostly new footage, offering a closer look at Ganondorf and showcasing the visual overhaul for several returning enemies.
The 30-second Battle commercial opens with Ganondorf playing the pipe organ. Close-ups of his fingers moving across the keys lead into a wider shot of the towering instrument. The footage appears to recreate the original N64 game’s pre-battle cutscene at the top of Ganon’s Tower, where Link discovers Ganondorf playing the organ immediately before their fight. The villain appears again later in the commercial, raising his hand as the Triforce mark glows with purple energy.

New Footage Teases A Few Bosses Like Morpha and Dark Link


Nintendo shows new footage that wasn't present in our last trailer breakdown. The new boss footage includes Morpha, the Water Temple’s boss, showing its watery tentacle wrapping around Link and lifting him off the platform, with the creature’s red weak spot visible inside the translucent water. Dark Link also appears in the Water Temple’s mist-covered arena, dodging Link’s sword thrust with a front flip and landing on top of the weapon.
Bongo Bongo gets a brief combat showcase of its own, with the Shadow Temple boss’s enormous disembodied hands attacking across the drum arena as Link dodges. The montage also includes Poe hunting on horseback at night in Hyrule Field, where Link can bottle and sell their souls for a hefty amount of Rupees in the original game.
Beyond the enemy encounters, the commercial shows Sheik being carried away by a shadowy attack. In the next shot, Link protects Sheik, sword drawn, as nearby structures burn. Finally, the closing sequence shows Link and Navi looking toward the imposing, burning castle as dark clouds gather above it.
Official commercials for the remake join the recent press preview, giving excited fans more snippets of the upcoming remake. In just three weeks, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launches on November 5, 2026, exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2. Pre-orders for the Zelda 2 anniversary Switch 2 and accompanying Amiibo are up now.
Source:
Nintendo Japan Ocarina of Time

item.title: Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Adds a Monster Museum With Timed Boss Rematches
item.description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake adds the Hall of Fallen Heroes, a new area where players can rematch bosses in a timed challenge. Find out more about the new mode below and other information from the recent hands-on preview.

The Hall of Fallen Foes Gives Hyrule’s Bosses A Second Round


Timed Boss Challenges Encourage Efficiency


The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s monsters are getting their own exhibition hall, giving players a new space to examine and rematch against the game's enemies. As shown in Nintendo’s newest overview trailer, released on October 14, 2026, the Switch 2 remake features the Hall of Fallen Foes.
This hidden location displays statues of enemies Link defeated throughout his adventure. Players can examine these statues for descriptions and information on where the creatures appear, but the main draw is the chance to challenge the game's bosses again.
King Dodongo demonstrates the feature in the video, with his entry offering a rematch button, a record of the player’s completion time, and an in-game timer overlaid during the battle. The trailer also offers glimpses of returning bosses, including Gohma, Phantom Ganon, Volvagia, and Twinrova.
Ocarina of Time 3D already offered a similar Boss Challenge mode, unlocked after clearing the Forest Temple and accessed by interacting with Link’s bed in Kokiri Forest to relive previous boss battles. These rematches were timed, and defeating all eight available bosses unlocked a gauntlet that challenged players to fight in succession. Other games in the franchise also featured timed boss challenges: Skyward Sword’s Thunder Dragon Lightning Round tracked boss clear times. At the same time, Echoes of Wisdom’s Slumber Dojo offered time-limited boss gauntlets and extra rewards for faster clears.

Hands-on Previews Reveal New Twists on a Familiar Hyrule


Ocarina of Time’s remake won’t be a 1:1 recreation of the original, with familiar environments, puzzles, and combat getting updates alongside its extensive visual overhaul. In our previous breakdown, we saw subtle changes like a bigger starting wallet, a possible fifth empty bottle slot, and enemies appearing in areas where they were originally absent.
Recently, Nintendo invited media outlets to play selected sections of the remake ahead of its release. Outlets report the preview ran roughly two hours and covered Kokiri Forest, the Great Deku Tree, Hyrule Field, Castle Town, and Adult Link’s Forest Temple. Those sessions revealed further changes in the remake, such as the Kokiri Sword chest, previously tucked into a corner of the boulder maze, now sitting on an elevated central platform players must jump to reach, as reported by IGN. In a separate breakdown, the site says the Forest Temple room now features guardrails that prevent Link from jumping onto a block before it rises toward the ceiling.
Nintendo Life reported that players can now summon a Business Scrub merchant inside dungeons using a Business Scrub Seed, which remains if they buy nothing. The Forest Temple also features a new lift in its block-pushing room, while the Poe picture puzzle no longer has a time limit. Additionally, jump attacks now involve a manual leap followed by a mid-air sword strike, instead of the previous Z-targeting and dedicated button to do the attack.
According to VGC, Hyrule's residents now have expanded dialogue and new interactions. In Kokiri Forest, a villager draws pictures of rupees and teaches a song that explains their value, while Castle Town’s bearded man now helps Link locate Talon by sensing other bearded people. Townspeople also display short dialogue bubbles as Link walks past, letting players catch their remarks without stopping to initiate a conversation.
These changes should freshen up Ocarina of Time for returning players, while new content like the Hall of Fallen Foes offers something extra for veterans who already know the 1998 original Hyrule by heart. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake releases exclusively on Switch 2 on November 5, 2026. Fans can now pre-order two new exclusive Ocarina of Time remake amiibos: Young Link and Young Zelda.
